sources.massKg: TUNING KNOB (cruise/ceiling) — 66 t operating mass, between OpenAP 737-800 OEW 41.4 t and MTOW 79 t (spec §3 ~79 t is the MTOW upper bound). Pinned by the FL350 cruise trim test; a typical mid-mission cruise weight.
sources.cl0: TUNING KNOB (cruise trim) — swept-wing zero-AoA lift; with clAlphaPerRad puts cruise AoA near 3 deg at M0.78/FL350.
sources.clAlphaPerRad: TUNING KNOB (cruise trim) — 5.5/rad (~0.096/deg), a swept transport-wing lift slope.
sources.stallAlphaRad: TUNING KNOB — 16.0 deg (0.28 rad) clean critical AoA; CLmax_clean = 0.2 + 5.5*0.28 = 1.74, a reasonable clean swept-wing maximum.
sources.postStallDecayRad: TUNING KNOB — 0.18 rad fade width past the break; a slightly sharper stall than the C172.
sources.cd0: TUNING KNOB (cruise Mach + service ceiling) — 0.020 clean parasite drag for a modern transport (OpenAP 737 clean CD0 ~0.018-0.022). Tuned so 85% thrust trims level at M0.78 at FL350 (measured M0.78) and the FL410 service ceiling still just climbs.
sources.oswaldE: TUNING KNOB — 0.80, typical transport span efficiency.
sources.cyBeta: TUNING KNOB — -0.9/rad transport side-force slope (large fin), so a slip bleeds energy.
sources.rollRateMaxRadS: TUNING KNOB (spec §3 large roll inertia) — 15 deg/s, deliberately low for the heavy-jet feel vs the C172's 40 deg/s.
sources.damping/stiffness: TUNING KNOBS (spec §3 large roll inertia): high rollDampingPerS with the low roll rate above gives the sluggish heavy-jet roll; pitch omega_n = sqrt(2.5) = 1.58 rad/s, zeta = 1.8/(2*1.58) = 0.57.
sources.refDynamicPressurePa: TUNING KNOB — 6000 Pa (~99 m/s at sea level); raised well above the C172's 1200 Pa because the jet flies much faster, so control authority saturates through the normal speed band.
sources.trimAlphaCenterRad: TUNING KNOB — 2.0 deg, near the cruise AoA so trim near centre is roughly hands-off cruise.
sources.trimAlphaRangeRad: TUNING KNOB — +-6.9 deg trim authority, enough to trim from approach AoA to cruise AoA.
sources.maxPowerW / propPeakSpeedMs: TUNING KNOBS (cruise Mach + service ceiling; decisions AF-004a) — a flat-rated turbofan is expressed through the shared power-limited-prop formula T = eta*P/max(V,propPeakSpeedMs): propPeakSpeedMs 260 m/s sits above max cruise TAS so thrust is CONSTANT with speed (T = eta*P/260), the flat-rated behaviour. maxPowerW 13.7 MW is a fictitious 'power' chosen so eta*P/260 = 0.85*13.7e6/260 = 44.8 kN full-throttle rated thrust — a realistic 737 cruise/climb thrust, NOT the ~2x107 kN static takeoff thrust (a constant-thrust prop formula cannot represent both, and this sim spawns airborne, so cruise thrust is what matters). Pinned so 85% throttle trims level at M0.78 at FL350.
sources.propEfficiency: 0.85 — the eta in T = eta*P/max(V,peak). Not a real prop efficiency (the 737 has no propeller); it is one factor of the fictitious eta*P product tuned, with maxPowerW, to the cruise thrust. Kept near 1 so maxPowerW carries the tuning.
sources.lapseModel: "turbofan" — selects forces.ts turbofanPowerLapse (flat-rated to TURBOFAN_CORNER_M, then density falloff). Chosen by this key, not a class branch; an absent/unknown value is a load-time validator error. Shared with the F-5E (Task 8): decisions AF-002.
sources.limits.vnoIasMs: 320 KIAS = 164.6 m/s, a display caution reference below Vmo.
sources.limits.vfeIasMs: ~250 KIAS = 128.6 m/s flap placard (most-restrictive detent); display only.
sources.serviceCeilingM: 41000 ft = 12497 m, 737-800 certified ceiling. Reached in-model via the shared turbofan thrust lapse (forces.ts, corner FL380 pinned by this target): full-throttle best climb there measures ~190 fpm (barely climbing), a real ceiling.
sources.flaps: 737 detents 0/1/2/5/10/15/25/30/40. dCL0/dStallAlpha/dCD0 are TUNING KNOBS giving monotonically falling stall speeds and rising drag across the schedule.
sources.display: ASI face 60-400 kt spans the jet band; attitudeStyle ball (full horizon disc for the airliner).
